primaryObjective: Determine whether the existing country assignments can gain reproducible, pinned administrative-boundary provenance without silently acquiring an unlicensed boundary dataset, weakening ocean or boundary ambiguity, or claiming subnational precision.
hypothesis: The current geography projection's 561,658 country assignments and 580,783 mapped boundary-provenance rows can support an explicit admin-0 release identifier, license, source hash, assignment algorithm, and stable boundary identifier for at least 548,257 catalog rows if the authoritative boundary release is already locally pinned and exactly reconstructible.

selectionRationale.reason: It is the highest-ranked unfinished data-first candidate after the accepted color assessment; the current ledger explicitly records zero administrative-region coverage while country assignment and generic boundary provenance are already present.

inScope: bounded inventory of local geometry, manifests, licenses, source URLs, hashes, assignment code, and country identifiers
deterministic parity audit between current geography assignments and any locally pinned boundary release
admin-0 assignment provenance sidecar or manifest only if exact reconstruction, license, hash, and ambiguity gates pass
country-level descriptive provenance coverage and export fields
one compact provenance disclosure only if every material gate passes
outOfScope: subnational or administrative-region assignment beyond the pinned geometry's verified level
whole-dataset external ingestion without public-domain status, compatible license, or permission
online geocoding, silent boundary substitution, nearest-country filling, coastline snapping, or disputed-territory guessing
mutating canonical coordinates or country labels
incidence, risk, causal, authenticity, or Pattern Finder claims

negativeControls: ocean and no-polygon rows remain unknown
exact reconstruction from the pinned local release
readinessContract.uncertaintyTreatment: Country assignment, administrative level, source geometry, disputed-territory policy, boundary-edge ambiguity, and coordinate precision remain separate. Missing provenance cannot be inferred from a country label alone.
readinessContract.suppressionPolicy: Publish a no-gain audit and do not deploy if the exact geometry release, rights evidence, stable identifiers, algorithm, or assignment parity cannot be proven locally. Never backfill from a different geometry release merely to satisfy coverage.

releaseGates: local provenance and rights reconciliation before any external query
exact pinned boundary release, source, license, hash, and stable identifiers
deterministic assignment reconstruction and country-code parity
ocean, disputed, edge, dateline, and high-latitude ambiguity preservation
complete Python and JavaScript suites if implementation occurs
browser QA, frozen preview-production parity, and tested rollback if a material gain is accepted
stopConditions: the current country assignments cannot be tied to one exact locally pinned boundary release
rights or redistribution evidence is missing or incompatible
stable boundary identifiers or assignment algorithm provenance are absent
exact reconstruction changes existing country assignments
coverage falls below 548257 rows without nearest-country or semantic guessing
scientific, provenance, rights, accessibility, or performance gates would need weakening
